parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence or documented traveller-facing universal exclusion/targeting. Laws prohibit anti-trans hate speech and discrimination, social attitudes are comparatively liberal with hostility concentrated among extremists, and the Pride attacker received the maximum sentence. Offsetting this, hate-crime reports rose while clearance fell to 45%, reporting is very low amid mistrust/dismissive treatment, and border, facilities, detention and visitor care are not documented—so functioning protection is only partially demonstrated.

entry_documents.interaction: No source addresses foreign-passport markers or border screening; absence is not treated as safety.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Custody placement not documented. Victims who report hate crimes describe dismissive treatment and mistrust of police.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Hate crimes motivated by gender identity/expression are recorded under the framework; a dedicated hate-crime group encourages reporting; Pride shooter received 30 years, the maximum.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Weak clearance and low reporting limit practical recourse if a visitor is detained after an attack.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: No documented bathroom/facility rule or identity-based facility access for visitors; no inference drawn.

care_services.exposure: Visitor emergency care and medication continuation not documented. Narrow resident gender-care access is resident-facing and not counted as a traveller exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Organised extremist and anti-trans feminist hostility, online threats, rising reported hate crimes, and intimidation risk especially at Pride; security service warns risks remain.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate speech covers transgender people since 2020; discrimination by gender identity/expression prohibited since 2013; prime minister publicly condemns anti-queer/trans hate.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing is protective, but falling clearance and concentrated extremist activism mean enforcement does not fully offset threat.

minors_guardians.interaction: Resident gender-recognition ages and same-sex relationship recognition do not establish a traveller-with-minor exposure or protection.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Record reports against queer/trans people in 2023; only 8% of LGBTQI hate-crime victims reported in survey; clearance fell 52% to 45% with more cases dropped. Incidents include a knife attack investigated as hate crime and online threats to a drag event.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2022 Pride mass shooter sentenced to 30 years, the strictest penalty; security service reports significant decline in threats over past year, most actors seeking fear rather than action.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Severe incidents occur but prosecution and declining threat assessments are positive response signals; low reporting means true volume is unknowable.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Official figures undercount offending; magnitude cannot be determined. Raw city counts lack per-capita denominators and cannot establish comparative risk.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Dedicated hate-crime group, hate-crime recording framework, and multi-thousand-person counter-signed feminist open letters indicate organised support, not a legal remedy.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknown visitor-facing practices for entry, facilities, custody and care prevent a higher score despite liberal social climate.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: acceptance plus legal protections and a conviction, with limited friction. Lower because this dossier lacks documented facility access, service-tribunal remedies, and detention individual assessment, and clearance is falling.

Higher than this case: 0.85-A directly documents accepted passports, identity-based facilities/wards, enforced service compensation and monitored custody. Here those traveller-facing positives are not documented and police follow-through is weaker.

Higher than this case: Pelora has documented border acceptance, no birth-sex exclusion, compensation and bias-assault prosecution despite border friction. This jurisdiction has stronger anti-discrimination/hate-speech law and liberal attitudes, but no documented visitor journey protections.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is legally protective and socially comparatively liberal, with hostility concentrated among extremists rather than diffuse street targeting, and a maximum-sentence prosecution after the Pride shooting. The traveller's residual risk comes from rising reported hate crime, falling clearance, low trust and dismissive reporting experiences, plus complete unknowns on entry, facilities, custody and emergency care. That places it in reduced risk, below cases where visitor-facing protections are directly demonstrated to work.
